text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Severity=sev2 · High tail latency on shared-gpu-pool-3 (p95/p99 breach). Auto-escalation to oncall.
sarah-p: ack, I'm awake. looking at dashboards now. can someone drop top tenants by qps? :coffee:
jamal: grabbing metrics — p95 jumped from ~200ms to 2.2s in the last 3m, p99 ~5.1s. Streaming stalls count spiked to 1200 (baseline 10)
eva-sre: logs show sustained NVME iowait on pool-3 hosts, and cgroup blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes is high for a few pods. suspect noisy neighbor batch jobs.
sarah-p: which pods? full list pls.
jamal: top consumers by blkio:
- tenant-acme-batch-12 (batch infer)
- tenant-lightbox-batch-04
- tenant-marketing-largejob
we're seeing `nvidia-smi` ok but `iostat -x` shows [%iowait] 42% on host gpu3-12
sarah-p: that explains streaming stalls — NVME IO stalls cascade into long queueing. evicting batch would help. I'll attempt a quick soft-evict on the biggest batch pod.
sarah-p: running: `kubectl -n inference delete pod tenant-acme-batch-12 --grace-period=30` (graceful) — moving to lower-priority queue
jamal: noted. also toggling routing to reduce pressure: switching 20% of traffic from shared-gpu-pool-3 to pool-1 (underutilized) via routing policy `redwood.routing/weights`
eva-sre: patching cgroup throttle as temporary mitigation: `kubectl exec -it node/gpu3-12 -- bash -c "echo 1048576 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/<id>/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device"` — applied to tenant-marketing-largejob. we'll monitor.
maria-support: heads up — two paid customers reported increased latency in last 10 minutes: Acme (critical) and Lightbox (paid). I'm on the support thread, will update customers after we have concrete ETA.
jamal: after evicting acme-batch pod p99 dropped to 1.1s within 60s, p95 ~400ms. streaming stalls down to 140.
sarah-p: nice. keep mitigation in place. need a more durable fix while we investigate root cause.
liam-ops: I'm going to move non-latency-sensitive batch workloads off shared pools during the incident window. scheduling migration job:
```
for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l job=batch -o name); do
  kubectl drain $pod --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  kubectl apply -f migration-target.yaml
done
```
liam-ops: started migration for tenant-lightbox-batch-04 and tenant-marketing-largejob
jamal: adding a temp alert: if blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes > 100MB/s for >30s then page SRE (severity=warning->page). this will prevent silent regressions.
eva-sre: collecting host-level traces and blkio counters. saving `iostat -x 1 30` and `dmesg` to /tmp/incident-1876543210.log
sarah-p: good. also enabling model-level fallback: route streaming requests to quantized-variant-v2 for tenants on pool-3 to reduce per-request IO (since quantized reads smaller weights).
jamal: executing routing change: `redwood route update --pool shared-gpu-pool-3 --percentage 30 --fallback quantized-variant-v2` — applied. expect to see lower read bandwidth per request.
maria-support: update for customers: "We identified noisy batch jobs causing IO contention on shared-gpu-pool-3. We've evicted heavy batch jobs and applied temporary throttles; latency is improving. We'll follow up with a timeline for permanent mitigations." customers acknowledged.
eva-sre: follow-up metrics: p95 ~310ms, p99 ~750ms after all mitigations. streaming stalls near baseline (20). writing artifacts to the incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1876543210/
liam-ops: will keep migrations running for next 20m. once pool-3 io stabilizes we'll gradually move traffic back.
sarah-p: note: root cause hypothesis = lack of IO QoS isolation on shared GPU hosts for batch pods (heavy sequential NVME write/read) that starve streaming pods. cgroup blkio write bps not set at job submission time.
jamal: actionable short-term items: 1) add admission webhook to require blkio limits for batch label 2) enforce QoS class best-effort->burstable mapping 3) add alert for host-level iowait > 30% impacting inference pools
maria-support: filed customer notes and escalations. will notify Acme separately once postmortem is ready.
liam-ops: oncall handoff: I'm taking over active watch for the next 2 hours (0400-0600 UTC). sarah, jamal — anything I should prioritize on handoff?
sarah-p: keep the migration until iowait < 10% for 10m and p99 < 500ms. if re-spike, evict remaining batch jobs and open a capacity bump with infra for more dedicated pools.
jamal: also run `kubectl top nodes` and watch nvme metrics; I've put a Grafana panel on the incident channel.
oncall-bot: HANDOFF: liam-ops is now oncall for this incident (start=1876543500). if situation escalates, page `#oncall` with `!page sev1`!
sarah-p: thanks — I'll pair on a quick runbook entry for noisy neighbor in the infra repo. follow-up owners: eva-sre (investigate host kernel configs), liam-ops (monitor & migrations), jamal (alerts & routing policy), maria-support (customer comms).
eva-sre: uploading logs and timeline to the incident doc. next steps: reproduce locally with synthetic IO-heavy batch to test limited blkio configs.
liam-ops: marking incident as mitigated for now. p95/p99 back within SLOs, streaming stable. keeping watch. will escalate if regression.
maria-support: customers updated. Acme requested postmortem. I've scheduled a customer call if needed.
sarah-p: closing follow-up action items in ops board. we'll do a postmortem tomorrow. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: deploy completed: routing rollback disabled -> confirmed stable (deploy-4592)
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> status=monitoring. incident file: s3://redwood-incidents/1876543210/notes.md
sarah-p: logging final note: severity downgraded from sev2 -> sev3 (monitoring). final p95=290ms p99=460ms. incident closed to active response. ongoing action items will be tracked in the postmortem.
